stem: Tiny config (|κ| = 6, U = 5), one core c = 0, no disputes. Block at slot 40: E_G carries guarantee g₁ for core 0. Block at slot 42: E_A has 4 assurances with bit 0 set. Block at slot 45: E_A has 3 assurances with bit 0 set and E_G carries an otherwise-valid guarantee g₂ for core 0. After the slot-45 block, what are ρ‡[0] and ρ′[0], and is g₁'s report ever accumulated?
options: ρ‡[0] = ∅ because 45 ≥ 40 + U; g₁'s report never enters W and is dropped without accumulation; g₂ is accepted, so ρ′[0] = (g₂, 45)
ρ‡[0] = (g₁, 40): the 4 + 3 = 7 assurances gathered so far exceed the threshold of 5, so the report is in W and accumulates, while g₂ is rejected as core_engaged
ρ‡[0] = ∅ because the cumulative 7 assurances made the report available; it accumulates in this block and ρ′[0] = (g₂, 45)
ρ‡[0] = (g₁, 40): the timeout only fires once H_t > t + U, i.e. from slot 46, so g₂ is rejected as core_engaged

stem: Full config (R = 10). The block being imported has τ′ = 57. For a guarantee g = (w, t, a) in E_G, which values of t are acceptable under eq. 11.28, and which assignment (M or M*) verifies the credential for each?
options: t ∈ [47, 57] — a sliding window of R slots ending at τ′; t ∈ [47, 49] is verified against M* and t ∈ [50, 57] against M; t = 46 is rejected as too old
t ∈ [40, 57]: t ∈ [40, 49] is verified against M* (rotation index 4) and t ∈ [50, 57] against M (rotation index 5); t = 39 and t = 58 are both rejected
t ∈ [50, 57] only — the current rotation, all verified against M — because M* is consulted solely when the previous rotation lies in the previous epoch
t ∈ [40, 59] — the whole previous and current rotation — with t > τ′ allowed since guarantees may be produced before the block that includes them

stem: Full config (E = 600, R = 10). A block at τ′ = 603 includes a guarantee with t = 595. Which assignment must its credential be checked against?
options: M* = (P(|κ′|, η′_2, 593), Φ(κ′)): the previous rotation always uses the current epoch's entropy and set, only the rotation index differs
M = (P(|κ′|, η′_2, 603), Φ(κ′)) at rotation index 0, because t is within R slots of τ′
The guarantee is invalid: a guarantee may not straddle an epoch boundary because the validator set may have changed
M* = (P(|λ′|, η′_3, 593), Φ(λ′)): the previous rotation (index 59) belonged to the previous epoch, so it is recomputed from λ′ and η′_3

stem: This is the team's P (GP 0.7.2). Under GP 0.8.0 (eq. 11.20–11.21), what changes when the validator sequence has |κ′| = 9 in a chain with C = 341 cores?
options: 0.8.0 builds the base [⌊i/3⌋ | i ∈ N_9] = [0,0,0,1,1,1,2,2,2] and rotates modulo |κ′|/3 = 3; this code builds ⌊341·i/9⌋ = [0, 37, 75, …, 303] and rotates modulo 341, scattering guarantors over inactive cores
Nothing observable: ⌊C·i/V⌋ and ⌊i/3⌋ coincide for every validator count permitted by eq. 6.8, and mod C equals mod V/3 for the same reason, so only the constant names differ between the versions
0.8.0 keeps ⌊C·i/V⌋ = [0, 37, 75, …, 303] as the base but changes the rotation modulus from C to E/R = 60, the number of rotations per epoch, so the shuffle output cycles once per epoch
0.8.0 replaces the Fisher–Yates shuffle by a plain rotation of the identity assignment [0, 1, 2, …, 8] modulo |κ′|/3, removing the dependence on η′_2 so that assignments are known a whole epoch ahead

stem: This is the team's refinement-context validation (GP 0.7.2). Which conditions required by GP 0.8.0 eq. 11.36 (anchor) and eq. 11.38 (lookup anchor) are missing from it?
options: Anchor: compare against β instead of β†, since 0.8.0 no longer patches the parent's state root into recent history; lookup anchor: unchanged, since the ancestor set already stores (slot, hash) pairs

Anchor: the context's anchor timeslot must also equal the β† entry's timeslot (x_t = y_t); lookup anchor: the child header h′ (h′_p = H(h)) must carry h′_r = l_s, verifying the lookup anchor's posterior state root
Anchor: drop the state-root comparison because 0.8.0 anchors carry a timeslot instead of a state root; lookup anchor: check only l_t ≥ H_t − L, since the ancestor-set requirement was removed in 0.8.0
Nothing beyond renaming BeefyRoot to the accumulation-output super-peak b, with the new BlockInfo timeslot being informational only; both anchor tuples are otherwise identical to 0.7.2

stem: Why can the lookup-anchor requirement (eq. 11.38) not be checked from the on-chain state σ alone, and how does the conformance fuzzer make it checkable for an M1 target?
options: It only needs β (the last H = 8 blocks, whose entries carry header hash and timeslot), so it is purely on-chain; the fuzzer merely replays enough blocks to fill β before testing guarantees
It needs the full posterior state of the lookup-anchor block (to recompute l_s), which the fuzzer supplies on demand through GetState messages during ImportBlock

It needs the headers of the last L slots (the ancestor set, not part of σ), deterministic from the header chain; the fuzzer's Initialize message therefore carries an ancestry list of (slot, header hash), a mandatory M1 feature
The fuzzer skips it: lookup anchors became optional in 0.8.0 (the refinement context may omit them), so only the age bound l_t ≥ H_t − L is exercised by the vectors

stem: A work-report in E_G lists prerequisite p. Package p was guaranteed 10 blocks ago and accumulated 8 blocks ago, so p ∈ ξ but p no longer appears in any entry of β (H = 8). Is the guarantee valid?
options: Valid: p ∈ ξ proves it was accumulated, so the dependency is satisfied and the report accumulates as soon as it becomes available
Invalid (dependency_missing): eq. 11.42 admits a prerequisite only if it is in this block's E_G or among the reported-package sets of β; ξ is not consulted at guarantee time
Valid, but the report is parked in the ready queue ϑ until p is reported again within the recent history
Invalid because a prerequisite must be guaranteed in the same block as the dependent report (only mutual and self dependencies are allowed)

stem: Service s upgraded its code after a work-package was built: the work-item's code hash c was correct at build time and refine ran the code available at the lookup anchor, but the including block's prior state has δ[s]_c ≠ c. What happens to the guarantee at inclusion?
options: Accepted: c only records which code refine executed (resolved at the lookup anchor), and accumulation uses δ′[s]_c regardless
Accepted, but the digest's result is replaced by the BAD error because the code preimage no longer matches the service
Accepted provided the lookup anchor is at most L slots old, since code availability is judged at the lookup-anchor state

Rejected (bad_code_hash): eq. 11.45 demands d_c = δ[d_s]_c in the prior state of the including block — c is a prediction of the code hash at reporting time, so a report refined against superseded code is discarded rather than accumulated

stem: Full config (C = 341). An assurer sets only the bit for core 340. What does E(f) look like, and what exactly does the assurer sign?
options: E(f) is 43 octets with last octet 0x08 (bits packed MSB-first within each octet); the signature is over X_A ⌢ H(H_p ⌢ E(f))
E(f) is 341 octets (one per core) ending in 0x01; the signature is over X_A ⌢ H_p ⌢ E(f) directly, without hashing
E(f) is 43 octets with last octet 0x10 (bit 4 of octet 42, LSB-first, no length prefix); the signature is over X_A ⌢ H(H_p ⌢ E(f)), i.e. a hash of 75 octets
E(f) is a length-prefixed sequence of 43 octets with last octet 0x10; the signature is over X_A ⌢ H(H_p ⌢ E(f))

stem: GP 0.8.0, C = 341, E = 600, R = 10. During epoch e the active set had |κ| = 12 (cores 0–3 active); at the epoch change the set shrinks to |κ′| = 9. The first block of the new epoch (τ′ = 600) carries a guarantee for core 3 with t = 595, signed by the three validators that M* assigns to core 3. Which statement is correct?
options: Valid: M* reproduces the previous rotation's assignment, under which core 3 was active, and the shard count |κ| = 12 was correct when the report was produced
Valid, but ρ′[3] is stored with the guarantee's own slot t = 595 as its timestamp, so it times out at the very next block

Invalid: eq. 11.28 requires w_c < |κ′|/3 = 3 with the posterior set even under M* — an inactive core may not be used even if it was active in the previous rotation; moreover (w_s)_n must equal |κ′| = 9 (eq. 11.31), and every pending entry of ρ‡ is cleared because |κ| ≠ |κ′| (eq. 11.18)
Invalid only because the signers come from λ′; a guarantee in an epoch's first block must be signed by members of κ′

stem: What does each entry of ρ (the availability assignments) hold in GP 0.8.0, and why did PR #494 change it?
options: ρ ∈ [(g ∈ G guarantee, t ∈ N_T timeslot)?]_C — the FULL guarantee including guarantor signatures plus the slot it was reported; kept so that the guarantors can be identified for fetching the bundle and for constructing culprits in a dispute
ρ ∈ [(w ∈ W work-report, t)?]_C — only the report and the slot, as in 0.7.x
ρ ∈ [H?]_C — only the report hash per core
ρ ∈ [(w, t, bitfield)?]_C — the report plus the running assurance bitfield

stem: A work-report W is a tuple (s, x, c, a, o, l, d, g). Which field description is WRONG?
options: s — the availability specification (package hash, bundle length, erasure root, shard count, segment root, segment count)
l — the segment-root lookup dictionary (work-package hash → segment root), which together with the prerequisites is limited to J = 8 entries
g — the total gas used by all refine invocations in the package
d — the work-digests, between 1 and I = 16 of them

stem: Which fields does the refinement context X contain in GP 0.8.0 (PR #526)?
options: Anchor: header hash a, timeslot t, posterior state root s, accumulation-output-log super-peak b; lookup-anchor: header hash l, timeslot l_t, posterior state root l_s; prerequisites p (a set of package hashes) — 8 fields
Anchor: header hash and state root; lookup-anchor: header hash and timeslot; prerequisites — 5 fields, as in 0.7.x
Anchor hash, anchor state root, BEEFY root, lookup-anchor hash, lookup-anchor slot, core index, prerequisites — 7 fields
Only the anchor hash and the prerequisites

stem: The availability specification s = (h, l, u, n, e, k). What are u, n, e and what constraint applies to n on-chain?
options: u = erasure root (Merkle root over the n erasure-coded chunks of bundle + exported segments); n = number of erasure shards, which must equal |κ′| (one chunk per assurer); e = segment root (constant-depth Merkle tree over exported segment hashes); k = segment count
u = segment root; n = number of work-items; e = erasure root; k = number of validators
u = bundle hash; n = 1023 always; e = exports root; k = core index
u = erasure root; n = number of guarantors (2 or 3); e = extrinsic root; k = chunk size

stem: A work-digest's result r ∈ B ∪ J where J = {∞, ☇, BADEXPORTS, OVERSIZE, BAD, BIG}. Which meaning is correct?
options: ∞ out-of-gas; ☇ panic; BADEXPORTS the number of exports was misreported; OVERSIZE the refine output would exceed the size limit; BAD service code unavailable at the lookup-anchor; BIG code exceeds W_C = 4,000,000
∞ infinite loop detected; ☇ host-call fault; BAD invalid signature; BIG bundle exceeds W_B
∞ out-of-gas; ☇ page fault; BAD the authorizer rejected the package; BIG too many work-items
All six are equivalent and simply mean the digest is empty

stem: What is the on-chain limit on the variable-size content of a single work-report?
options: |authorizer trace o| + Σ over digests of |result blob| (errors count as 0) ≤ W_R = 48·2^10 = 49,152 octets
Each digest's output ≤ 4 KiB and at most 16 digests
The encoded report ≤ W_B = 13,791,360 octets
|o| ≤ 32 and each result ≤ W_G = 4,104 octets

stem: Which set of rules applies to the assurances extrinsic E_A?
options: Each assurance = (anchor a, bitfield f ∈ bits[C], validator index v, Ed25519 sig); a must equal H_p; assurances strictly ordered by v (so at most one per validator); the signature by κ[v]_e is over X_A ⌢ H(E(H_p, f)); a bit may be set only if ρ†[c] ≠ ∅
Assurances are anchored on the block's own hash and signed with Bandersnatch keys
Any number of assurances per validator; the bitfield has one bit per validator
Assurances are signed over the erasure root of each report; ordering is by core index

stem: When does a report become available (W), and when is a pending assignment cleared from ρ‡ in GP 0.8.0?
options: Available iff the number of assurances with bit c set is > 2/3·|κ| (tiny: ≥ 5 of 6; full: ≥ 683); ρ‡[c] = ∅ if the report became available, or H_t ≥ t + U (U = 5 slots), or |κ| ≠ |κ′| (the validator-set size changed)
Available iff ≥ 1/3·|κ| assurances; cleared after U = 10 slots
Available iff exactly 2/3·|κ| assurances; never cleared until accumulated
Available iff > 1/2·|κ| assurances; cleared on every epoch change

stem: How are validators assigned to cores for guaranteeing in GP 0.8.0?
options: P(v, e, t) = R(F([⌊i/3⌋ | i ∈ N_v], e), ⌊(t mod E)/R⌋): the sequence [0,0,0,1,1,1,…] is Fisher-Yates shuffled with entropy e = η′_2, then rotated by the rotation index (R = 10 slots); M = (P(|κ′|, η′_2, τ′), Φ(κ′)) — only cores < |κ′|/3 are active
Validator i is assigned to core i mod C, rotating one core per block
P uses η′_1 and rotates every epoch; all 341 cores are always active
Assignment is by Bandersnatch VRF: each validator picks its own core

stem: Which statement about a guarantee g = (w, t, a) in E_G is correct?
options: a has 2 or 3 (validator index, Ed25519 sig) pairs ordered by index; each signer must be assigned to core w_c under M (if t is in the current rotation) or M* (previous rotation); R·(⌊τ′/R⌋ − 1) ≤ t ≤ τ′; the signature is over X_G ⌢ H(E(w)); w_c < |κ′|/3; E_G is ordered & unique by core
a has exactly 3 signatures; t must equal τ′; the signature is over the encoded report itself
a has 1 signature from the block author; t may be any slot in the last 24 hours
Signers may be any validators in κ′ ∪ λ′; E_G is ordered by report hash

stem: Which on-chain checks apply to each incoming report w before it is placed in ρ′?
options: ρ‡[w_c] = ∅ (core free after assurances/timeouts); w_a ∈ α[w_c] (authorizer in the PRIOR pool); Σ digest accumulate-gas ≤ G_A = 10,000,000 and each digest's gas ≥ δ[s]_g (the service's minaccgas); erasure shard count = |κ′|
ρ[w_c] = ∅ (prior); w_a ∈ α′[w_c]; Σ gas ≤ G_T
The core must have been free for at least U slots; total gas ≤ G_R = 5·10^9
The report must be signed by the manager service

stem: Which of the following is NOT one of the contextual validity requirements for reports in E_G?
options: No two reports in the extrinsic share a work-package hash, and no package hash may appear in β's reported sets, in ξ (accumulated), in ϑ (ready queue) or in ρ (pending)
The anchor (a, s, b, t) must match an entry of β†; the lookup-anchor time ≥ H_t − L and the lookup-anchor must be in the ancestor set A
Every prerequisite and every segment-root-lookup key must be in this extrinsic or in β's reported sets, and lookup segment roots must match
Each digest's service must have been accumulated within the last epoch, otherwise the report is rejected

stem: After processing E_G, what does ρ′[c] hold for a core that received a new guarantee g?
options: (g, τ′) — the full guarantee with the current block's timeslot as the assignment time, so it can be timed out if not assured within U slots
(g, g_t) — the guarantee with the guarantee's own slot t
(w, 0) — the report with a zeroed timestamp
The report hash only; the guarantee itself is discarded

stem: The team's availability check uses `totalAvailable[i] >= types.ValidatorsSuperMajority`. Which statement is accurate?
options: It is equivalent to the GP's strict '> 2/3·|κ|' as long as ValidatorsSuperMajority = ⌊2|κ|/3⌋ + 1 is derived from the actual size of κ (5 for 6 validators, 683 for 1023); for 0.8.0 it must follow |κ| rather than a compile-time constant
It is wrong: the GP requires ≥ 2/3·|κ|, so 4 of 6 should suffice in tiny
It is wrong: the GP counts assurances per validator, not per core
It is wrong: reports on cores where rhoDagger[i] == nil should still be added

stem: What are ξ (accumulated) and ϑ (ready) and how big are they?
options: ξ ∈ [{H}]_E — one set of accumulated work-package hashes per slot for the last E = 600 slots (an epoch of history); ϑ ∈ [[(W, {H})]]_E — per slot, the reports made available in that slot that still have unfulfilled dependencies, each paired with its outstanding dependency set
ξ ∈ {H} — all package hashes ever accumulated; ϑ ∈ [W] — a FIFO of all pending reports
ξ ∈ [{H}]_H — 8 slots of history; ϑ ∈ [(W, N)]_C — one queued report per core
ξ and ϑ are both dictionaries from report hash to timeslot

stem: How is the sequence of accumulatable reports W* built from the newly available reports W?
options: W! = reports with no prerequisites and empty segment-root lookup, accumulated immediately; W^Q = the rest, each paired with its dependency set (prerequisites ∪ keys of srlookup) pruned by ξ_∪; W* = W! ⌢ Q(E(ϑ[m..] ⌢ ϑ[..m] ⌢ W^Q, P(W!))) where Q repeatedly extracts reports whose dependency set is empty and E removes satisfied dependencies
W* = W sorted by core index; dependencies are checked by guarantors, not on-chain
W* = all of ϑ followed by W; a report with a missing dependency causes the block to be invalid
W* = W! only; queued reports are accumulated one epoch later regardless of dependencies

stem: What total gas budget g is handed to the outer accumulation Δ+ in a block, and how does Δ+ choose how many reports to accumulate in a round?
options: g = max(G_T, G_A·C + Σ_{x∈values(χ_Z)} x); Δ+ picks the largest prefix i of the reports such that Σ digest gas-limits of those i reports + Σ gas of pending deferred transfers + Σ free-accumulation gas ≤ g, runs Δ* on them, then recurses with g* = g + Σ(new transfers' gas) − Σ gas actually used and an empty free-accumulation map
g = G_T = 3.5·10^9 always; Δ+ accumulates all reports regardless of gas
g = G_A = 10^7 per report; Δ+ accumulates reports one at a time
g = G_R = 5·10^9; Δ+ stops at the first report whose service panics

stem: In Δ* (parallel accumulation), which services are accumulated and how are the privileged indices (assigners, delegator, registrar) resolved when both the manager and the privileged service itself change them?
options: s = {services with a digest} ∪ keys(f) ∪ {destinations of deferred transfers}; each is accumulated exactly once via Δ1; the manager's output decides χ′_M and χ′_Z; for assigners/delegator/registrar R(o, a, b) = b if a = o else a — i.e. the manager's change wins unless the manager left it unchanged, in which case the service's own change applies
Only services with digests are accumulated; privileges can only be changed by the manager
Every service in δ is accumulated each block; privilege conflicts make the block invalid
Services are accumulated in order of service index; the last writer of a privilege wins

stem: For a single service s, Δ1 invokes Ψ_A(e, τ′, s, g, i^T ⌢ i^U). How is the gas g computed and what are the inputs?
options: g = f[s] (free allowance, or 0) + Σ gas of deferred transfers destined to s + Σ accumulate gas-limits of s's digests across the round's reports; i^T = the transfers to s (in order), i^U = one operand tuple per digest of s (report order)
g = G_A = 10^7 fixed; inputs are the raw work-reports
g = δ[s]_g (the service's minaccgas); inputs are only the digests, transfers are delivered separately via on_transfer
g = the service's balance in gas units; inputs are the exported segments

stem: A deferred transfer T = (s, d, a, m, g). What are the fields, and when is the balance moved?
options: s source service, d destination, a amount, m memo of W_T = 128 octets, g gas limit for the recipient's handling; the sender's balance is deducted when `transfer` is called, and the amount is credited to the destination when it is accumulated in a later round
s sender's Ed25519 key, d destination, a amount, m message hash, g gas price; settled immediately
s source, d destination core, a amount, m memo of 32 octets, g gas refund
Transfers are settled off-chain by guarantors

stem: After Δ+ returns (n, e′, b, u, t), which statements about the final integration are correct?
options: θ′ = the (service, hash) pairs in b (services that yielded a 32-byte hash); (δ‡, ι′, φ′, χ′) come from e′; the accumulation statistics record per service (N items accumulated, T transfers processed, G gas used); δ‡‡ marks a_a = τ′ for every service that appears in the statistics; ξ′[E−1] = P(W*[..n])
θ′ = the hash of the whole δ‡; ι′ is unchanged until the next epoch; ξ′ is reset to empty
θ′ = b; statistics record only gas; a_a is updated for all services in δ
The outputs are discarded; only the new balances matter

stem: Which rule governs the preimages extrinsic E_P and its integration into δ′?
options: E_P ∈ [(s, d)] ordered & unique; each (s, d) must be providable in the PRIOR δ — the service exists and δ[s]_l[(H(d), |d|)] = [] (requested, not yet provided); integration happens after accumulation: δ′ = I(δ‡‡, E_P), setting a_l[(H(d),|d|)] = [τ′] and a_p[H(d)] = d, silently dropping any preimage that is no longer useful
Any preimage may be included; unrequested ones are stored for 24 hours
E_P is integrated before accumulation so that accumulate can read the new preimages
Preimages must be signed by the service's manager

stem: This is the team's prefix selection in Δ+. Compared with GP 0.8.0 eq. 12.17, what is missing?
options: 0.8.0 requires the budget test to include Σ gas of the pending deferred transfers t and Σ free-accumulation allowances f (Σ d_g + Σ t_g + Σ f ≤ g), so gasSum must start from those two sums rather than 0
Nothing — the loop exactly matches eq. 12.17
The loop should break as soon as a single report exceeds G_A = 10^7
